design_note: Fresh post-v0.5.4 wording and compositions. No item in this set was used to implement v0.5.4. Any later tuning makes this set regression-only.

items.evidence_text: For treatment initiation, renal function from eGFR 30 through 45 falls in the not-recommended interval; the contraindication begins when eGFR is less than 30.
items.candidate_claim: For a new patient with eGFR 44, initiation is not recommended by this rule.

items.evidence_text: The label separates two renal actions: initiation is not recommended at eGFR 30 to 45, while use is contraindicated only below 30.
items.candidate_claim: A new patient at eGFR 31 meets the contraindication threshold.

items.evidence_text: For someone already receiving therapy, an eGFR that falls under 45 prompts benefit-risk reassessment. Discontinuation is specified only when the value is under 30.
items.candidate_claim: At eGFR 44, an existing user falls under the reassessment rule rather than the discontinuation threshold.

items.evidence_text: Existing users below eGFR 45 require reassessment of benefit and risk; stopping is reserved for eGFR values below 30.
items.candidate_claim: Every existing user whose eGFR is 44 must discontinue immediately.

items.evidence_text: The renal section provides rules for initiation, reassessment and discontinuation, but this excerpt gives no instruction for an eGFR value that has not been measured.
items.candidate_claim: Without a measured eGFR, this excerpt alone determines that the patient must discontinue therapy.

items.evidence_text: An NSAID taken during anticoagulant therapy is associated with a higher bleeding risk.
items.candidate_claim: Concomitant NSAID use is associated with increased bleeding risk during anticoagulant therapy.

items.evidence_text: The source reports higher bleeding risk with NSAID co-use but does not state that the combination is forbidden in all patients.
items.candidate_claim: The combination is prohibited in every patient according to this source.

items.evidence_text: The interaction evidence supports greater bleeding risk with NSAID exposure. It provides no basis for ranking men above women or women above men in risk.
items.candidate_claim: NSAID exposure raises bleeding risk, and women have the highest risk compared with men.

items.evidence_text: The current label states that condition K by itself does not constitute a contraindication to treatment A.
items.candidate_claim: Condition K alone makes treatment A contraindicated under the current label.

items.evidence_text: This excerpt discusses condition K but contains no statement about whether K is or is not a contraindication to treatment A.
items.candidate_claim: Condition K is a contraindication to treatment A.

items.evidence_text: Spontaneous safety reports can be useful for identifying a signal that merits further evaluation; an individual report cannot distinguish causal attribution from mere temporal association.
items.candidate_claim: A spontaneous reporting system can contribute to signal detection without establishing causality from a single report.

items.evidence_text: A single spontaneous report may raise a safety signal, but it cannot distinguish causation from association on its own.
items.candidate_claim: One spontaneous report proves that the product caused the event.

items.evidence_text: The spontaneous-report database has no complete denominator of exposed patients, and reporting is incomplete; raw report counts therefore cannot yield the event rate in treated patients.
items.candidate_claim: Raw report counts can be converted directly into the true event incidence in treated patients.

items.evidence_text: The reporting database lists 240 reports, but the excerpt supplies neither a complete exposed-population denominator nor a validated incidence estimate.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports that 240 reports were observed, but it does not supply the true incidence.

items.evidence_text: The trial registry lists the study as ACTIVE, NOT RECRUITING and identifies the prespecified primary outcome. No study-result value is present in the supplied record.
items.candidate_claim: The registry supports the study status and identifies the primary outcome, without establishing its achieved result.

items.evidence_text: The registration record gives the planned primary outcome and recruitment status; no outcome result is included in this evidence bundle.
items.candidate_claim: The registration record demonstrates that the primary outcome was successfully achieved.

items.evidence_text: The study is listed as COMPLETED. Its primary endpoint is named, but the supplied registry material contains no result showing whether the endpoint was met.
items.candidate_claim: The study is completed and its primary endpoint was met.

items.evidence_text: The registry reports that the study is COMPLETED and provides the primary endpoint definition; the result field is absent from this excerpt.
items.candidate_claim: The study is completed and the primary endpoint definition is available.

items.evidence_text: Guideline H explicitly replaces Guideline G as the operative recommendation source for the current version.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline H is the operative current source and Guideline G is no longer current.

items.evidence_text: Guideline H explicitly replaces Guideline G for current recommendations.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline G remains the operative current recommendation after H replaces it.

items.evidence_text: Guideline H is current. This evidence does not mention Guideline F or specify any relationship between F and H.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline H superseded Guideline F.

items.evidence_text: A randomized trial published after the guideline favors option Q, but the guideline has not been updated and remains operative with recommendation P.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence landscape now includes randomized support for Q, while the current guideline still recommends P.

items.evidence_text: A new randomized trial postdates the current guideline and favors Q; the guideline itself remains unchanged and recommends P.
items.candidate_claim: Publication of the trial automatically rewrites the current guideline recommendation from P to Q.

items.evidence_text: The new trial favors Q, while the current guideline still recommends P. The evidence supplied here does not state when a guideline update will occur.
items.candidate_claim: The trial favors Q and the current guideline still recommends P, and the guideline will be updated next month.

items.evidence_text: Drug M inhibits CYP3A, and Drug N is a CYP3A substrate. This establishes a plausible pharmacokinetic interaction mechanism but supplies no product-specific dose instruction.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports a plausible CYP3A-mediated pharmacokinetic interaction between M and N.

items.evidence_text: Drug M inhibits CYP3A and Drug N is a CYP3A substrate; no clinical contraindication or required dose change is stated in this passage.
items.candidate_claim: The mechanism alone establishes that M and N are clinically contraindicated together.

items.evidence_text: A genotype is associated with increased drug exposure. The source does not provide a genotype-specific dose recommendation.
items.candidate_claim: The genotype is associated with increased exposure, but the appropriate dose is not determined by this source.

items.evidence_text: The genotype is associated with higher exposure, and no therapeutic dosing rule is given in the evidence supplied.
items.candidate_claim: The genotype is associated with higher exposure, so every carrier must receive half the standard dose.

items.evidence_text: A retrospective cohort observed an association between exposure L and outcome R. The design cannot distinguish a causal effect from confounding.
items.candidate_claim: The cohort supports an association between L and R but does not establish that L causes R.

items.evidence_text: A retrospective cohort found L associated with R, but the design cannot separate causation from confounding.
items.candidate_claim: The cohort proves that L causes R.

items.evidence_text: The report classifies the lesion as indeterminate and recommends contrast-enhanced MRI for characterization. It does not establish malignancy.
items.candidate_claim: The lesion is indeterminate and contrast-enhanced MRI is recommended for further characterization.

items.evidence_text: The report describes an indeterminate lesion and recommends MRI; malignancy is not established in the report.
items.candidate_claim: The lesion is indeterminate and MRI is recommended, but the report proves the lesion is malignant.

items.evidence_text: The pathology summary explicitly classifies finding X as benign.
items.candidate_claim: The pathology summary classifies finding X as malignant.

items.evidence_text: The report states that finding X is benign and gives no recommendation for biopsy in the supplied excerpt.
items.candidate_claim: Finding X is benign, and the report mandates immediate biopsy.

items.evidence_text: Two separate studies report response rates of 71% and 54%, but the populations differ and there is no randomized head-to-head comparison.
items.candidate_claim: The studies report different response percentages, but they do not provide a randomized direct superiority comparison.

items.evidence_text: Separate studies report 71% and 54% response rates in different populations, without a randomized head-to-head comparison.
items.candidate_claim: The 71% response rate alone proves treatment A is superior to treatment B.

items.evidence_text: Evidence supports association C with outcome D. The source contains no subgroup analysis comparing association strength in urban versus rural participants.
items.candidate_claim: Evidence supports association C with D, and the association is stronger in urban than rural participants.

items.evidence_text: Evidence supports association C with D, and a prespecified subgroup analysis reports a stronger association in urban than rural participants.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports association C with D and reports a stronger association in urban than rural participants.

items.evidence_text: The evidence explicitly states that biomarker J is not associated with outcome W in this analysis.
items.candidate_claim: Biomarker J is associated with outcome W in this analysis.

items.evidence_text: The excerpt reports biomarker J levels but provides no analysis of association between J and outcome W.
items.candidate_claim: Biomarker J is not associated with outcome W.
